Doctor of Philosophy in Computer Science
Location(s): Glassboro Campus
Return to: Programs of Study
The PhD in Computer Science is a rigorous, research-focused program designed to prepare students for leadership roles in academia, industry, and government. Students in the program develop a deep understanding of computer science theories and methodologies, and they conduct original research to contribute to the advancement of knowledge in the field. The program includes coursework in advanced topics such as algorithms, artificial intelligence, machine learning, computer systems, and software engineering.
PhD candidates are required to complete comprehensive exams, engage in research seminars, and write a dissertation that demonstrates the ability to conduct independent research. The program emphasizes problem-solving, critical thinking, and the development of innovative solutions to complex technical challenges. Graduates are well-prepared for academic positions, research roles in industry, or advanced technical leadership positions in the growing field of computer science.
Required Courses: 12 s.h.
A grade of B or higher is required in all Required Courses used to fulfill this section.
Computer Science Theory and Algorithms: Must take one
CS 04548 - Programming Languages: Theory, Implementation and Application Credits: 3
CS 07510 - Mathematical Foundations of Computer Science Credits: 3
CS 07622 - Advanced Theory of Computing Credits: 3
CS 07540 - Advanced Design and Analysis of Algorithms Credits: 3
Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning: Must take one
CS 02505 - Data Mining I Credits: 3
CS 07556 - Machine Learning I Credits: 3
CS 07650 - Concepts in Artificial Intelligence Credits: 3
Systems and Infrastructure: Must take one
CS 02530 - Advanced Database Systems: Theory and Programming Credits: 3
CS 06560 - Design and Implementation of Operating Systems Credits: 3
CS 09510 - Computer Networks Credits: 3
Required Course:
CS 99700 - Research Methods Credits: 3
Required Field of Study Courses: 12 s.h.
Each student, in consultation with their thesis advisor, is required to select a required field of study that will consist of 12 credits of courses. These courses cannot overlap with the courses chosen to satisfy the Required Courses above; however, they may be selected from the Required Courses and Elective Courses banks. Required courses and field of study courses will provide the students with the minimum breadth of knowledge in the field of computer science needed to successfully conduct research in the chosen area of study.
Elective Courses: 21-27 s.h.
A minimum of 21 and a maximum of 27 semester hours of elective coursework are required. Courses will be recommended by a student’s thesis advisor to align with their research area. Elective courses and thesis research must total 51 semester hours. The distribution between these two areas will be determined by the student and their thesis advisor. Elective courses are 3 credits each and may be taken from this Elective bank or the Required Courses bank, but courses cannot overlap with the courses chosen to satisfy the Required Courses above.

Thesis Research: 21-27 s.h.
A minimum of 21 and a maximum of 27 semester hours of thesis research are required. Thesis research and elective courses must total 51 semester hours. The distribution between these two areas will be determined by the student and their thesis advisor. See advisor for information regarding the Research and Dissertation course.
CS 02799 - Doctoral Research and Dissertation Credits: 1 to 9
Total Required Credits for the Program: 72 s.h.
Complete and Pass Annual Progress Reports: evaluated by the student’s graduate faculty committee and research advisor
Pass a Qualifying Exam
The Qualifying Exam has two parts, intended to assess the fitness of students for the program.
Part 1: GPA requirement:
Students must earn a B or higher in all 12 credits of required coursework.
Part 2: Research potential:
Students will prepare an oral presentation and written report on a research area of interest. A committee of faculty members in the student’s area of interest will assess the student’s work and assign a “pass” or “fail” grade. Subject to the approval of the formed committee, Part 2 can be waived by strong evidence of research potential (e.g., students can use relevant first-authored peer-reviewed publications related to the Field of Study to waive Part 2).
Pass a Dissertation Proposal Exam
The Dissertation Proposal Exam consists of an oral presentation and a written report detailing the student’s achieved and proposed research work toward the PhD. A committee of faculty members in the student’s area of research will evaluate the Dissertation Proposal and determine a “pass” or “fail” grade.
Successfully defend their Dissertation
Minimum Required Grades and Cumulative GPA
The Ph.D. in Computer Science is a Category 3 program.
For details regarding Graduate Policies and Procedures, please visit:
https://sites.rowan.edu/student-success/graduate-student-information/graduate-policies.html
